Duration: 8 Month Contract (FTE conversion is possible but based on needs of the business at the time)

Pay Rate: $80–85/hr

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM



Overview

Seeking an experienced Electric Rates professional to support electric rate design, analysis, and implementation, with a focus on regulatory filings and proceedings. The ideal candidate will have experience with electric rate design within an investor-owned utility, preferably in California, along with strong Excel skills and experience preparing regulatory testimony.



Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, analyze, revise, and administer electric tariff schedules.
  • Compile, analyze, and maintain rate, revenue, load, and customer data to evaluate existing tariffs and support proposed rate changes.
  • Conduct detailed rate analysis and develop financial/rate models to support pricing decisions and regulatory filings.
  • Support CPUC regulatory filings and proceedings, including preparing written testimony and responding to data requests.
  • Support leaders with mass rate impact and comparison projects, ensuring timely and accurate results.
  • Perform standard to complex rate analysis for non-residential customers and develop tailored solutions.
  • Review rate change applications for accuracy, compliance, and strategic alignment.
  • Collect and analyze financial information and operating statistics to inform regulatory strategies.
  • Maintain and enhance rate analysis tools, models, and internal calculators.
  • Support the development of special contract rates for current and prospective customers.
  • Prepare written assessments and present recommendations to leadership and executive-level stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop and implement processes and solutions.
  • Identify methodological issues and develop appropriate solutions using professional judgment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.



Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required; preferably in Economics, Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
  • Typically 5+ years of related experience in electric rates, rate analysis, pricing, or a similar utility function.
  • Previous electric rate design or implementation experience with an investor-owned utility, preferably in California.
  • Experience actively participating in or leading regulatory proceedings.
  • Experience writing regulatory testimony and responding to regulatory data requests.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including experience developing and maintaining rate/pricing models.
  • Knowledge of integrated rate development, cost allocation, and cost recovery processes.
  • Knowledge of regulatory, contractual, and policy requirements affecting electric rates.
  • Strong analytical and project management skills.
  • Ability to independently manage defined rate analysis workstreams.
  • Ability to influence decisions through data-driven analysis and insights.

Preferred Experience

  • California utility regulatory experience.
  • CPUC regulatory filing experience.
  • Non-residential/commercial electric rate analysis.
  • Rate impact and comparison analysis.

job.title: Senior Civil & Structural Engineer – Power Generation
job.description:
Senior Civil & Structural Engineer – Power Generation

Location: Dallas, TX
Employment Type: Permanent / Full-Time
Salary: $175,000–$195,000 base + performance-based bonus
Relocation: Assistance available

We are seeking an experienced Senior Civil & Structural Engineer to provide technical leadership across the development and execution of complex power generation projects.

This position will support projects incorporating gas turbines, utility-scale solar and battery energy storage systems (BESS), with responsibility for coordinating and overseeing civil, structural and geotechnical engineering throughout project development, design, EPC execution and construction.

Working from the owner's side, you will provide technical oversight of EPC contractors and engineering consultants while managing civil, structural and geotechnical risks that could impact project cost, schedule or constructability.

Key Responsibilities

Civil Engineering

  • Coordinate and oversee civil engineering activities performed by EPC contractors and engineering consultants.

  • Review site layouts, grading, earthworks, roads, drainage and underground utility designs.

  • Ensure civil designs meet project requirements and integrate effectively with the overall power plant design.

  • Review flood protection, stormwater management, erosion control and site access requirements.

  • Support optimization of site layouts, grading and earthwork quantities to reduce project cost, schedule and construction risk.

  • Participate in design reviews, value engineering and constructability assessments.

Structural Engineering

  • Coordinate structural engineering activities across power generation facilities.

  • Oversee foundation design for gas turbines, generators, transformers and other balance-of-plant equipment.

  • Review structural steel, pipe rack, building and equipment support designs.

  • Support structural requirements associated with solar and BESS installations.

  • Review engineering calculations, drawings and specifications for technical accuracy and code compliance.

  • Review geotechnical investigations and ensure recommendations are appropriately incorporated into foundation and structural designs.

  • Coordinate structural interfaces with equipment vendors, including equipment loads, anchor bolts and embedments.

  • Ensure effective coordination between civil, structural, mechanical and electrical engineering disciplines.

  • Verify designs against applicable ASCE 7, ACI 318 and AISC 360 requirements and site-specific wind, seismic and soil conditions.

EPC & Consultant Management

  • Serve as the civil and structural engineering coordination lead when working with EPC contractors.

  • Define scopes of work and review technical proposals from engineering and geotechnical consultants.

  • Oversee the quality, schedule and technical performance of EPC and consultant deliverables.

  • Participate in multidisciplinary design reviews, constructability reviews and project risk assessments.

  • Identify and resolve civil, structural and geotechnical issues throughout engineering, procurement and construction.

  • Ensure civil and structural requirements are properly integrated across the wider project.

Construction & Project Support

  • Provide technical support during construction and assist with resolution of field engineering issues.

  • Review civil and structural design changes for technical, cost and schedule impacts.

  • Support constructability assessments and value engineering initiatives.

  • Coordinate technical interfaces between site contractors, EPC teams, equipment vendors and engineering consultants.

  • Help identify and mitigate civil, structural and geotechnical risks before they impact project execution.

Regulatory, Documentation & Risk Management

  • Support coordination with regulatory authorities and other stakeholders regarding civil and structural design approvals.

  • Assist with responses to technical comments and information requests.

  • Maintain appropriate technical studies, calculations, drawings and engineering documentation.

  • Report on design progress and emerging technical risks.

  • Provide civil and structural input into project schedules, budgets and risk registers.

  • Support technical inputs for project development reports, internal approvals, financing and due diligence activities.

Required Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering or a related engineering discipline.

  • Approximately 7–10+ years of civil and structural engineering experience supporting power generation or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects.

  • Experience overseeing or coordinating EPC contractors and engineering consultants.

  • Strong knowledge of civil site development, grading, drainage, earthworks and underground infrastructure.

  • Experience with structural steel and foundation design for major industrial equipment and facilities.

  • Strong understanding of geotechnical considerations and their impact on foundation and site design.

  • Knowledge of applicable structural design codes including ASCE 7, ACI 318 and AISC 360.

  • Experience reviewing engineering calculations, drawings, specifications and other design packages.

  • Strong technical review, coordination and communication skills.

Preferred Experience

  • Simple-cycle or combined-cycle gas turbine power generation experience.

  • Utility-scale solar and/or BESS project experience.

  • Experience reviewing civil and structural design packages during EPC execution.

  • Owner/developer-side power generation experience.

  • Experience with STAAD.Pro, SAP2000, AutoCAD Civil 3D or similar engineering tools.

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification.

  • Field engineering or construction experience on major power or industrial projects.

Why Join?

This is an opportunity to take significant technical ownership across major energy infrastructure projects, working closely with project leadership, EPC contractors, engineering consultants and equipment vendors.

The position offers a $175,000–$195,000 base salary, performance-based bonus opportunity, potential sign-on support and relocation assistance for candidates moving to the Dallas area.

If you have a strong background in civil and structural engineering for power generation or large industrial infrastructure and want to take an owner-side role across the full project lifecycle, we would like to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Mechanical Project Engineer – Gas Turbine
job.description:
Senior Mechanical Project Engineer – Gas Turbine Power Generation

Location: Dallas, TX
Employment Type: Permanent / Full-Time
Salary: $160,000–$190,000 base + performance-based bonus
Relocation: Assistance available

We are seeking an experienced Senior Mechanical Project Engineer to provide technical leadership across the development, design, procurement, construction and commissioning of gas turbine power generation projects.

This is an owner-side engineering position with significant technical responsibility. You will act as a key technical authority for gas turbine generation facilities, working closely with equipment OEMs, Owner's Engineers, EPC contractors and internal project stakeholders to ensure projects achieve their performance, reliability, schedule and lifecycle objectives.

The ideal candidate will bring extensive experience within gas turbine power generation, with strong knowledge of turbine packages, auxiliaries, balance-of-plant systems and EPC project execution.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as a technical lead for mechanical systems associated with gas turbine power generation facilities.

  • Provide owner-side engineering oversight throughout project development, procurement, EPC execution, commissioning and operation.

  • Support the definition, design and integration of gas turbines and associated auxiliary systems.

  • Oversee mechanical equipment packages, piping layouts and balance-of-plant interfaces.

  • Review and validate engineering deliverables including PFDs, P&IDs, equipment data sheets, specifications and thermal system documentation.

  • Perform and review engineering assessments including heat and mass balances, thermal performance evaluations and water/heat balance calculations.

  • Support technology selection and configuration studies across simple-cycle, combined-cycle and other power generation solutions.

  • Develop technical requirements, specifications and performance guarantees for major equipment procurement and EPC contracting.

  • Lead technical evaluations of OEM and EPC proposals and support commercial and contractual negotiations.

  • Manage technical interfaces with equipment manufacturers, EPC contractors, consultants and other project stakeholders.

  • Evaluate technologies designed to improve plant output, efficiency, reliability and emissions performance.

  • Support emissions control strategies, air permitting and environmental compliance requirements.

  • Participate in HAZOP, HAZID and other technical and operational risk reviews.

  • Review EPC design packages, installation procedures and commissioning plans.

  • Participate in Factory Acceptance Tests, Site Acceptance Tests, performance testing and reliability testing.

  • Support resolution of technical issues during construction, start-up and commissioning.

  • Provide ongoing engineering support for operating assets, including troubleshooting, upgrades, outage planning and performance optimization.

Required Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.

  • Significant engineering experience within the power generation industry, ideally 10+ years, although candidates with 7+ years of highly relevant experience may be considered.

  • Direct gas turbine power generation experience is essential.

  • Strong technical understanding of gas turbine packages, auxiliaries and balance-of-plant interfaces.

  • Experience supporting power generation projects through development, design, EPC execution and/or commissioning.

  • Experience working with equipment OEMs, EPC contractors and multidisciplinary engineering teams.

  • Strong understanding of mechanical plant systems, piping, equipment integration and technical specifications.

  • Experience reviewing engineering drawings and documentation including PFDs and P&IDs.

  • Knowledge of power plant environmental, emissions and regulatory requirements.

  • Strong technical communication skills with the ability to work effectively with engineering, commercial and executive stakeholders.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience working for an IPP, power project developer, owner/operator, EPC organization or major equipment OEM.

  • Simple-cycle and/or combined-cycle gas turbine project experience.

  • Field commissioning, start-up or performance testing experience.

  • Experience with air permitting and emissions control technologies including SCR and oxidation catalysts.

  • Understanding of HRSG and steam-cycle integration.

  • Exposure to advanced power generation technologies, carbon capture readiness or hydrogen blending.

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license.

Why Join?

This is an opportunity to take a senior technical role in the delivery of major power infrastructure projects while working directly with project leadership, OEMs and EPC partners.

The position offers a $160,000–$190,000 base salary, performance-based bonus opportunity, potential sign-on support and relocation assistance for candidates moving to the Dallas area.

If you have a strong background in gas turbines and power generation engineering and want to take greater technical ownership across the full project lifecycle, we would like to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Electrical Engineer – Power Generation
job.description:
Senior Electrical Engineer – Power Generation

Location: Dallas, TX
Employment Type: Permanent / Full-Time
Salary: $160,000–$190,000 base + performance-based bonus
Relocation: Assistance available

We are seeking an experienced Senior Electrical Engineer to take ownership of the electrical scope across the full lifecycle of complex power generation projects, from conceptual design and FEED through detailed engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning and energization.

Working on projects incorporating gas turbines, utility-scale solar, battery energy storage systems (BESS) and other power generation technologies, you will provide technical leadership across electrical system design, power distribution, grid integration, equipment selection and project execution.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced power systems engineer to take an owner-side role with significant responsibility across the development and delivery of large-scale energy infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

Conceptual Design & FEED

  • Develop preliminary single-line diagrams, electrical layouts and system architectures for power generation projects.

  • Define HV and MV power distribution strategies and network configurations.

  • Perform and review load flow, fault and short-circuit studies.

  • Assess transformers, switchgear, power conversion equipment and other major electrical systems.

  • Evaluate grid interconnection requirements and applicable electrical standards.

  • Assess reactive power, harmonics and system stability requirements.

  • Develop protection philosophies and preliminary relay strategies.

  • Prepare equipment specifications and procurement requirements for major electrical assets.

  • Support feasibility studies, CAPEX/OPEX estimates and technical evaluations.

  • Coordinate with mechanical, civil and controls engineering disciplines to develop fully integrated project solutions.

Detailed Design & EPC Execution

  • Coordinate and oversee the development of IFC electrical engineering deliverables by EPC contractors.

  • Review detailed single-line diagrams, protection and control schematics, cable schedules, grounding designs and electrical layouts.

  • Review protection coordination, arc flash and grounding studies.

  • Review and approve EPC engineering calculations, drawings and technical documentation.

  • Manage electrical design changes and assess potential technical, cost and schedule impacts.

  • Ensure designs comply with project specifications, utility requirements and applicable IEEE, IEC and NEC standards.

Procurement & Vendor Management

  • Prepare technical requisitions and bid evaluations for transformers, switchgear, MCCs, inverters, BESS and generator electrical packages.

  • Review vendor drawings, calculations and technical documentation.

  • Participate in Factory Acceptance Tests (FATs).

  • Resolve technical queries with equipment vendors and EPC contractors.

  • Support equipment procurement and expediting activities.

Construction & Commissioning

  • Provide electrical engineering support during construction and resolve field engineering issues and RFIs.

  • Conduct site inspections and technical reviews of electrical installations.

  • Verify installation of cabling, terminations, switchgear, transformers and grounding systems against approved designs.

  • Support QA/QC activities, punch-list management and mechanical completion walkdowns.

  • Develop and review commissioning plans, testing procedures and energization sequences.

  • Support Site Acceptance Tests (SATs), protection relay testing and functional testing.

  • Support system energization, grid synchronization and performance testing through project handover.

  • Review as-built documentation and support technical project closeout.

Required Experience

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems Engineering or a related discipline.

  • Ideally 10+ years of engineering experience within power systems, although candidates with 7+ years of highly relevant experience may be considered.

  • Strong experience within power generation, utility-scale renewable energy or industrial power systems.

  • Experience across multiple stages of the project lifecycle, including conceptual design, FEED, detailed engineering/EPC, construction and commissioning.

  • Strong understanding of HV/MV electrical system design, protection schemes and grid integration.

  • Experience with power system analysis software such as ETAP, PSCAD or equivalent.

  • Experience producing or reviewing single-line diagrams, protection schematics, cable schedules and grounding designs.

  • Knowledge of applicable IEEE, IEC and NEC requirements.

  • Working knowledge of construction, QA/QC, commissioning and testing of HV/MV electrical systems.

  • Ability to coordinate effectively with EPC contractors, equipment vendors and multidisciplinary engineering teams.

Preferred Experience

  • Gas turbine power generation experience is highly desirable.

  • Utility-scale solar PV and/or BESS project experience.

  • Experience working within an owner/operator, IPP, power project developer or EPC organization.

  • Experience with FEED studies for power generation, microgrid or renewable energy projects.

  • Grid interconnection and power system studies experience.

  • Field experience during construction, commissioning and energization.

  • AutoCAD or similar electrical design software experience.

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license, or ability to obtain one.

Why Join?

This is an opportunity to take significant technical ownership across major power infrastructure projects while working closely with project leadership, EPC contractors, equipment suppliers and multidisciplinary engineering teams.

The position offers a $160,000–$190,000 base salary, performance-based bonus opportunity, potential sign-on support and relocation assistance for candidates moving to the Dallas area.

If you have a strong background in power systems engineering, power generation, gas turbines, solar or BESS and want to work across the complete project lifecycle, we would like to hear from you.

job.title: Onboarding Engineer
job.description:
Onboarding Engineer
Palm Beach Gardens, FL (100% on-site)
Duration: initial 12-month contract
Pay: $37-42/hr

We are seeking an experienced Electrical/Power Systems Engineer to support the onboarding of renewable generation and battery energy storage facilities into utility operations and NERC compliance programs. This role will lead the technical review, validation, and acceptance of engineering and NERC compliance evidence before and after Commercial Operation Date (COD).

Responsibilities

  • Lead technical review of engineering and NERC compliance documentation for renewable generation and battery energy storage facilities.
  • Review PSSE, PSLF, and PSCAD power system models and verify consistency with equipment data, electrical drawings, field settings, commissioning results, and as-built configurations.
  • Interpret one-line/three-line diagrams, transmission and substation drawings, equipment specifications, transformer parameters, cable/impedance data, and other electrical documentation.
  • Review NERC MOD-related testing and model verification, including plant controller, inverter, protection/relay settings, short-circuit, reactive capability, and ride-through studies.
  • Identify discrepancies between models, drawings, equipment, settings, studies, and test results and coordinate resolution with Engineering, Operations, OEMs, consultants, Transmission Owners, ISO/RTOs, and NERC Compliance teams.
  • Track technical requirements and deliverables through pre-synchronization, COD, and post-COD closeout.
  • Support technical evaluations related to applicable NERC BAL, EOP, FAC, MOD, PRC, and VAR requirements.
  • Develop automation and reporting solutions using Python, Power Automate, and Power BI to improve evidence tracking, validation, reconciliation, and project visibility.
  • Utilize Maximo and develop repeatable engineering processes to improve onboarding consistency across the renewable fleet.
  • Apply engineering judgment to determine whether technical evidence is complete, accurate, and sufficient for onboarding requirements.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in electrical engineering, power systems, renewable generation, utility operations, or a related field.
  • Strong understanding of power system engineering, electrical equipment, protection and controls, and utility-scale generation.
  • Experience reviewing electrical drawings, equipment specifications, power system studies, commissioning documentation, and test results.
  • Experience with power system modeling tools such as PSSE, PSLF, and/or PSCAD.
  • Knowledge of NERC standards and compliance requirements, particularly MOD-related modeling, testing, and model verification.
  • Experience with renewable generation, inverter-based resources, and/or battery energy storage systems preferred.
  • Proficiency with Python, Power Automate, Power BI, or similar tools for automation, data analysis, and reporting preferred.
  • Strong analytical, documentation, problem-solving, and cross-functional communication skills.
  • Ability to independently evaluate technical information, identify discrepancies, and drive resolution with internal and external stakeholders.

job.description:
Location: Draper, UT (Onsite)

Schedule: Standard

Duration: 6 Month W2 Contract

Pay Rate: $25.70/hr

Position Summary

In this role, you will set up and run a range of machine tools to produce precision parts and instruments. You will also fabricate and modify parts used to build and repair tools and machinery. Day to day, that means reading blueprints and technical drawings, calculating dimensions and tolerances, setting up fixtures and cutting tools, and keeping an eye on feeds and speeds while parts are being machined. Quality is a big part of the job. You'll measure, inspect and test finished parts to make sure they meet specifications before they move on. You'll also help maintain the shop's industrial machines so they stay running reliably. This role suits a hands-on machinist with 2-4 years of experience who is precise, works well on their own and enjoys solving problems at the machine. NIMS certification is a plus.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

  • Calculate dimensions and tolerances using shop math and precision instruments such as micrometers and vernier calipers
  • Align and secure holding fixtures, cutting tools, attachments, accessories and materials on machines
  • Monitor machine feeds and speeds throughout the machining process
  • Measure, inspect and test finished parts to catch defects and confirm they meet specifications
  • Set machine controls, and enter, retrieve or edit commands in computerized machine control programs
  • Maintain industrial machines, using knowledge of mechanics, shop mathematics, metal properties, layout and machining procedures

Education/Experience

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • 2-4 years of machining experience required
  • NIMS license/certification preferred

Knowledge/Skills

  • Strong verbal communication, attention to detail and problem-solving skills
  • Able to work independently and manage your own time
  • Basic knowledge of raw materials, production processes, quality control and other methods for efficient manufacturing and distribution
  • Basic knowledge of the design techniques, tools and principles used to produce precision technical plans, blueprints, drawings and models
  • Basic knowledge of machines and tools, including their design, use, repair and maintenance

job.description:
Title: Oligonucleotide / Peptide Purification Development

Location: Cambridge, MA

Pay: $48.00-$55.00/hr

Schedule: Standard Office Hours

Duration: 6-Month Initial Contract




We are seeking a highly motivated and creative scientist or engineer with process development experience to join an Oligonucleotide / Peptide Purification Development team. This position offers the opportunity to develop robust, high-purity purification processes for oligonucleotide and peptide therapeutics and gain hands-on exposure to the design, development, scale-up, and transfer of manufacturing processes supporting clinical and commercial programs.

The successful candidate will contribute to the development of novel purification technologies and processes, working across laboratory, pilot-scale, and manufacturing environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and characterize purification processes for oligonucleotide and peptide therapeutics, including process development, process characterization, robustness studies, and scale-up.
  • Support purification unit operations including chromatography, detritylation, and ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF).
  • Utilize multiple chromatography modes and support or learn additional processing steps including chemical cleavage, conjugation, and hybridization.
  • Investigate novel purification technologies and approaches designed to improve purity, process robustness, and productivity.
  • Support early- and late-stage process characterization and robustness studies.
  • Scale up and transfer oligonucleotide purification processes into pilot-scale and GMP manufacturing facilities.
  • Contribute to technology transfer activities, manufacturing documentation review, troubleshooting, and on-the-manufacturing-floor support.
  • Support root cause investigations and process evaluations, working independently where appropriate with guidance from the supervisor.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with teams supporting synthesis, drug product, analytical development, research, manufacturing, project management, and technology transfer.
  • Document laboratory and development activities through development reports and other technical documentation.
  • Lead or support pilot-scale activities and small, focused technical initiatives.
  • Provide training and mentoring to new employees as appropriate.
  • Participate in the preparation and authoring of CMC/regulatory sections for IND submissions.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience successfully planning and executing scientific projects and experiments.
  • Hands-on laboratory experience with the purification of proteins, peptides, and/or DNA/RNA.
  • Experience using column chromatography, such as:
    • Ion exchange chromatography
    • Hydrophobic interaction chromatography
    • Reversed-phase chromatography
  • Experience with ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF).
  • Hands-on experience analyzing proteins, peptides, and/or DNA/RNA, preferably using HPLC and UV/Vis spectroscopy.
  • Demonstrated technical proficiency and creativity in developing or evaluating purification technologies and approaches.
  • Strong organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and within cross-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ÄKTA purification systems and UNICORN software.
  • Experience with Design of Experiments (DoE).
  • Experience with statistical analysis.
  • Experience with process scale-up, technology transfer, or GMP manufacturing environments is beneficial.

Education & Experience

Associate Scientist 3 / Engineer 2

  • Bachelor’s degree in Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, or a related life science field with 2–4 years of industry experience; or
  • Master’s degree in a related field with 0–2 years of industry experience.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, or a related life science field with 4+ years of industry experience; or
  • Master’s degree in a related field with 2+ years of industry experience.

job.description:
CQV Engineer – Pharmaceutical Manufacturing

Location: Clayton, North Carolina
Contract: 24 months, with potential for extension
Pay Rate: $65/hour
Work Model: On-site

We are seeking an experienced CQV Engineer to support commissioning, qualification, and validation activities across pharmaceutical manufacturing projects in Clayton, NC.

The CQV Engineer will lead validation efforts for assigned projects from requirements definition through qualification, validation, change control, and decommissioning. Projects may involve facility systems, aseptic formulation and filling, medical device assembly, packaging, warehouse and QC operations, manufacturing systems, and computerized equipment.

This position requires previous pharmaceutical validation experience and the ability to independently develop and execute validation deliverables following an initial onboarding period.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead commissioning, qualification, and validation activities for assigned pharmaceutical manufacturing projects.

  • Develop, revise, and maintain validation plans, reports, specifications, risk assessments, traceability matrices, and decommissioning documentation.

  • Author and execute Design Qualification/Review, Installation Qualification (IQ), Operational Qualification (OQ), Performance Qualification (PQ), and Process Validation protocols and reports.

  • Support commissioning and qualification activities to ensure equipment and systems are ready for validation execution.

  • Participate in Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) where required.

  • Track validation documentation, milestones, risks, and deliverables across multiple concurrent projects.

  • Provide regular project status updates and escalations to Project Managers.

  • Identify, investigate, and document deviations and engineering changes encountered during validation.

  • Initiate, author, and support Change Controls and assess the validation impact of proposed changes.

  • Participate in recurring project meetings and lead focused validation meetings when required.

  • Use electronic validation and quality systems such as TIMS/HP ALM and Veeva QualityDocs/Vault Quality.

  • Ensure validation activities comply with GMP, FDA requirements, EU Annex 15, GAMP 5, and applicable company procedures.

  • Support project activities during plant shutdowns, which may occasionally require evening or weekend work.

Preferred Experience

Candidates with pharmaceutical validation experience in one or more of the following areas are particularly relevant:

  • Manufacturing equipment upgrades and production line modifications

  • Aseptic formulation and filling equipment, including RABS

  • Vision inspection systems

  • Medical device assembly equipment

  • Pharmaceutical packaging equipment

  • Process control and manufacturing execution systems, including SCADA, PLC, PAS-X, and LMES

  • Laboratory and GMP facility modifications

  • Process instrumentation, monitoring, and calibration systems

  • BMS, HVAC, refrigeration, and facility utility systems

  • Electrical distribution, switchgear, and controls

  • Physical security, access control, and CCTV systems

  • Technology modernization and lifecycle replacement projects

  • Electronic validation documentation and execution

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience generating and executing validation documentation within a pharmaceutical or regulated GMP manufacturing environment.

  • Hands-on experience with commissioning, qualification, and validation activities.

  • Strong knowledge of IQ/OQ/PQ, risk assessments, traceability, deviations, and change control.

  • Understanding of applicable GMP, FDA, EU Annex 15, and GAMP 5 requirements.

  • Ability to independently manage validation deliverables across multiple projects after onboarding.

  • Strong technical documentation, communication, and project coordination skills.

  • Ability to work on-site in Clayton, North Carolina.

  • Flexibility to support occasional evening or weekend activities during major project execution or plant shutdowns.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced CQV or Validation Engineer to join a long-term pharmaceutical manufacturing program and work across a diverse portfolio of equipment, facility, automation, and manufacturing projects.

job.description:
Business Data Analyst – Utility Operations

Location: Pomona, California
Work Model: Hybrid – Onsite Monday & Tuesday
Schedule: Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM
Contract: 12 months
Pay Rate: $38.60/hour

We are seeking an experienced Business Data Analyst to support the planning, execution, reporting and analysis of electric utility inspection programs.

This position supports multiple Distribution and Transmission programs, including detailed asset inspections, annual grid patrols, streetlight patrol surveys, infrared scanning and intrusive pole evaluations.

The Business Data Analyst will work across program management, inspection planning, data analysis and exception processing, partnering with contractors and internal stakeholders to ensure inspection scopes are accurately planned, tracked and completed.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support planning and scheduling for internal and external inspection teams across multiple electric utility programs.

  • Manage schedules covering data collection, processing, contractor deliverables, quality assurance, risk assessment and delivery of inspection results.

  • Develop, maintain and distribute progress and performance reports.

  • Lead and participate in meetings throughout the inspection lifecycle, from initial data collection through risk review and final distribution.

  • Coordinate activities and communications between contractors and internal stakeholders.

  • Support financial planning, cost analysis and execution for inspection programs.

  • Create accurate scope packages and work orders in accordance with applicable requirements and guidelines.

  • Work with inspection and planning teams to improve scoping strategies and operational efficiency.

  • Maintain lessons learned, change control logs and planning documentation.

  • Track constrained inspections and access issues to mitigate compliance and scheduling risks.

  • Identify required follow-up actions and coordinate resolution across stakeholders.

Data Analysis & Reporting

  • Produce regular daily and weekly performance reports, dashboards and ad hoc analyses.

  • Monitor inspection performance and completion against established scopes and deadlines.

  • Analyze financial and cost data and investigate discrepancies identified internally or by contractors.

  • Research data discrepancies across SAP, inspection applications and reporting platforms.

  • Analyze historical performance by structure, region, resource and inspection type.

  • Identify synchronization and data-quality issues and coordinate resolution with business and IT teams.

  • Analyze trends in inspection and survey results.

  • Validate that inspection data is accurately populating reporting dashboards.

  • Develop and improve data-management tools that provide timely and accurate status reporting.

  • Use mapping and spatial data to identify potential access constraints and support inspection planning.

  • Create and analyze KMZ files and spatial joins for locations including government lands and other constrained areas.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Statistics or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

  • Approximately 5-7 years of analytical experience.

  • Demonstrated ability to perform moderately complex quantitative and data analysis.

  • Experience gathering, documenting and analyzing information and translating findings into actionable conclusions.

  • Strong data-management skills, including data querying, reporting and data controls.

  • Experience developing dashboards and data visualizations.

  • Strong project and issue-tracking capabilities, from identification and root-cause analysis through resolution.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to work across multiple teams, subject matter experts, contractors and stakeholders.

Technical Skills

Experience with several of the following is preferred:

  • SAP

  • Power BI

  • SQL

  • SAS / SAS Visual Analytics

  • Microsoft Excel and MS Office

  • Python

  • Snowflake

  • ArcGIS

  • Data visualization and dashboard development

Experience navigating SAP work orders, maintenance plans, measurement documents, functional locations (FLOCs) and equipment data is particularly relevant.

ArcGIS experience involving the joining and analysis of mapping layers such as districts, functional locations, circuits and constrained areas is also highly desirable.

Work Environment

This is a hybrid position based in Pomona, California, with onsite attendance required Monday and Tuesday. Candidates should be comfortable working across technical, operational and business teams in a data-intensive utility environment.

job.title: Senior Mechanical Project Engineer
job.description:
Job Type: Full-Time
Industry: Power Generation / Energy

We are seeking a Senior Owner’s Engineer to provide technical leadership for gas turbine power generation projects from early-stage development through EPC execution, commissioning, and long-term asset optimization.

This is a highly technical, owner-side role for an experienced power-generation engineer with strong knowledge of open-cycle/simple-cycle gas turbines, balance-of-plant systems, equipment integration, EPC execution, and OEM management.

Key Responsibilities

Owner’s Engineering & Technical Leadership

  • Serve as the technical lead and subject matter expert for gas turbine generation projects.
  • Provide owner-side oversight of gas turbines and major auxiliary systems, including fuel gas, lubrication, hydraulics, inlet air, exhaust, cooling, emissions controls, fire protection, and black-start systems.
  • Ensure equipment and plant designs support long-term reliability, availability, maintainability, and operating economics.
  • Manage technical interfaces between the owner, EPC contractor, OEMs, equipment suppliers, and other project stakeholders.

Engineering & Project Development

  • Establish technical requirements, equipment specifications, performance requirements, and project boundary conditions.
  • Lead conceptual design, feasibility studies, technology evaluations, and project development activities.
  • Review and validate engineering deliverables including PFDs, P&IDs, equipment datasheets, specifications, heat and mass balances, and performance calculations.
  • Support selection and evaluation of simple-cycle, combined-cycle, CHP, and emerging power-generation configurations.

Technology & Efficiency

  • Evaluate technologies that improve plant efficiency, flexibility, output, and emissions performance.
  • Support assessments involving inlet air chilling, turbine power augmentation, thermal storage, intercooling, ORC, and other advanced technologies.
  • Lead technical evaluations of emissions-control technologies including SCR and CO/oxidation catalysts.
  • Support decarbonization initiatives, including carbon capture readiness and hydrogen blending.
  • Provide technical input into CAPEX, OPEX, lifecycle economics, and business-case development.

OEM, Procurement & EPC Management

  • Develop technical specifications, RFQs, bid requirements, and performance guarantees for major equipment and EPC contracts.
  • Lead technical evaluations of OEM and EPC proposals.
  • Manage technical deviations, change orders, warranties, and long-term service agreement interfaces.
  • Provide owner-side oversight throughout engineering, procurement, construction, installation, and commissioning.

Risk, Compliance & Permitting

  • Participate in HAZOP, HAZID, and other formal project risk reviews.
  • Identify and mitigate technical, operational, safety, and reliability risks.
  • Support air permitting, emissions modeling, and environmental compliance activities.
  • Ensure projects meet applicable EPA, state/local, environmental, safety, and industry requirements.

Commissioning & Operations

  • Participate in FATs, SATs, startup, commissioning, and performance testing.
  • Lead resolution of technical issues involving OEMs, EPC contractors, and equipment suppliers.
  • Provide ongoing engineering support to operating assets, including troubleshooting, outage planning, performance optimization, upgrades, and reliability improvements.
  • Evaluate retrofit and modernization opportunities to improve efficiency, emissions performance, and long-term asset value.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
  • 10+ years of experience in gas turbine power generation, power project development, EPC execution, OEM engineering, or owner/operator environments.
  • Strong technical knowledge of open-cycle/simple-cycle gas turbines and balance-of-plant systems.
  • Experience with gas turbine auxiliaries, equipment integration, and mechanical/piping systems.
  • Experience reviewing PFDs, P&IDs, equipment specifications, datasheets, and thermal/performance documentation.
  • Experience with OEM and EPC contractor management.
  • Knowledge of emissions-control systems and air permitting requirements.
  • Experience supporting project development, procurement, commissioning, or plant operations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working for an IPP, power developer, utility, or owner/operator organization.
  • Simple-cycle and/or combined-cycle project execution experience.
  • Experience with HRSG/steam-cycle integration.
  • Gas turbine OEM experience with companies such as GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Ansaldo, or similar.
  • Experience with air permitting and emissions compliance.
  • Knowledge of hydrogen blending, carbon capture, power augmentation, or other decarbonization technologies.
  • Field commissioning, startup, and performance testing experience.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred.

We are looking for a capable and hands-on Financial Accountant to join our team in a role that combines traditional finance responsibilities with ERP implementation and business systems support.

You will work closely with Finance, Operations, IT and external implementation partners to help ensure that our new systems, processes and reporting are fit for purpose.

The ideal candidate will be a strong accountant who is also systems-minded, analytical, organised and comfortable working through problems and testing new processes.

Key Responsibilities



Finance & Accounting

  • Support day-to-day financial accounting and finance operations.
  • Assist with month-end and year-end close processes.
  • Prepare and review account reconciliations and financial reports.
  • Assist with general ledger, journals, accruals, prepayments and other accounting activities.

ERP Implementation & Systems

  • Assist with data migration activities, including data validation and reconciliation.
  • Review and document business processes and system procedures.
  • Work with implementation partners, consultants and internal stakeholders to track issues through to resolution.
  • Support system cutover, go-live and post-implementation activities.
  • Help develop user guides, process documentation and training materials.
  • Act as a key link between the Finance team and ERP/IT stakeholders.



About You

We are looking for someone who combines strong accounting fundamentals with an interest in technology and business systems.

You will ideally have:

  • Relevant accounting qualifications or significant accounting experience.
  • Experience working in a Financial Accountant or similar finance role.
  • Strong understanding of general ledger, month-end close, reconciliations and financial reporting.
  • Experience with an ERP system such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dynamics AX, SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Pronto, TechnologyOne or a similar platform.

  • The ability to understand both finance processes and how those processes translate into an ERP system.
  • Strong communication skills and the confidence to work with Finance, IT, Operations and external consultants.
  • A proactive attitude and willingness to get involved and solve problems rather than simply identify them.



What We Offer

  • A broad and varied role across Finance and business systems.
  • The opportunity to play a key role in an ERP transformation.
  • Exposure to Microsoft Dynamics 365 and modern finance technology.
  • The opportunity to work closely with senior Finance, Operations and IT stakeholders.
  • A role with genuine scope to improve processes and ways of working.
  • Support and development as you build your ERP and systems expertise.

Role

Key responsibilities

· Analyse investment and portfolio data to support investment teams and business decision-making.

Ideally, you will bring:

· Strong investment domain knowledge, ideally from superannuation, asset management or investment management.

Senior Embedded Software Engineer

My client has an immediate requirement for an experienced Senior Embedded Software Engineer to join their team on an initial 3-month contract, with a strong possibility of extending for a further 9–12 months.

Key details

  • Role: Senior Software Developer / Embedded Software Engineer
  • IR35: Inside IR35
  • Start: Ideally 1 October, but ASAP for the right person
  • Initial duration: 3 months, with a strong possibility of extension
  • Location: Motherwell / Glasgow, Scotland
  • Working pattern: Hybrid

    • Further afield: 2–3 days per month in the office may be considered for the right candidate

The role

You’ll be working on embedded C software development for a benchtop medical device used in the diagnosis and management of medical conditions.

The team is working towards 510(k) FDA approval, followed by the commercial release of the software and bootloader. You’ll work within a regulated development environment alongside a wider engineering team, using tools including Jira, Jama, Confluence and Git.

Must-have experience

  • Experience with IEC 62304 or other relevant medical device software standards
  • Experience creating software requirements
  • Experience with unit testing frameworks, such as Unity or CMock
  • Experience working in Agile/Scrum environments
  • Experience with tools such as Jira and Git

Nice to have

  • Experience creating and maintaining software systems
  • Embedded GUI development and GUI frameworks
  • Experience with Python, R or other high-level languages for data processing

Sector experience

  • Medical devices / MedTech
  • Regulated environments
  • FDA / 510(k) experience would be beneficial

The key requirement is someone who is genuinely strong in Embedded C, has worked in a regulated software environment, and can get up to speed quickly on a medical device development programme.

job.title: Supplier Warranty Engineer
job.description:
Supplier Warranty Engineer
Normal, IL (100% on-site)
Duration: initial 6-month contract
Pay: $55-60/hr

We are seeking a Supplier Warranty Program Specialist to support the technical management and continuous improvement of a Supplier Warranty Partnership Program. This role will serve as a key connection between warranty data analysis, parts returns, supplier quality engineering, and the supplier network.

The position will focus on analyzing warranty data, identifying supplier-related trends and issues, supporting corrective actions, and driving improvements that reduce warranty costs and improve overall product quality.

Responsibilities

  • Support the technical execution and continuous improvement of the Supplier Warranty Partnership Program.
  • Partner with Supplier Quality teams to develop, retrieve, and analyze field data to identify opportunities to improve product quality and reduce warranty costs.
  • Drive continuous improvement through supplier corrective action processes, including warranty-related corrective action requests.
  • Collaborate with data and analytics teams to establish data requirements and improve the speed and accuracy of addressing supplier warranty concerns.
  • Develop and track Supplier Warranty KPIs across vehicle and product programs while driving organizational awareness of performance.
  • Conduct ad-hoc data analysis and technical deep dives into vehicle issues, warranty trends, and service center operations.
  • Maintain accurate warranty evidence, supplier agreement data, claims information, and performance metrics.
  • Generate recurring reports and dashboards using analytics tools such as Hex, Databricks, and other data platforms.
  • Analyze supplier warranty data to identify trends, root causes, improvement opportunities, and areas for optimization.
  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders to collect relevant data and maintain alignment with program objectives.
  • Communicate with suppliers to gather required information, resolve discrepancies, and address warranty-related issues.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with technicians, engineers, customer service teams, and other stakeholders to improve warranty data quality and support program objectives.
  • Manage multiple projects and initiatives across different teams and geographic locations.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline; Master’s degree preferred.
  • 4+ years of experience working with automotive supplier warranty data and statistical analysis.
  • Strong statistical analysis, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience with data visualization and analytics tools such as Hex and Databricks.
  • Familiarity with JIRA and other software/data management tools.
  • Knowledge of AIAG, VDA, APQP, and related automotive quality methodologies.
  • Demonstrated experience driving quality improvements and improving overall vehicle or product performance.
  • Strong technical knowledge with the ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, manufacturing, supplier, and quality organizations.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively in a highly cross-functional environment.
